questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I have family in Berlin, and thus wanted to try living in the city. This was the most important aspect.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I loved every second and can definitely recommend going to Berlin and Humboldt!

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I found the whole process a bit confusing, as you need to send a lot of the same information in different formats to different receivers. I got a bit overwhelmed, but in the end, you get mails every step of the way taking you through the process, and that made it doable. My advice is: just do as the emails says, and don't stress too much about is! :)

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not really any.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Hugs are very helpful! They are a team at Humboldt helping exchange students, and they have different ways of helping out and making social connections. I definitely recommend using them as much as needed.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Very difficult, very expensive. I used
wunderflats.de
, but they have changed their design, and are now way more expensive, so I wouldn't advice to use that now. Honestly not sure how I would go about it today.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's hard to find and expensive! Be prepared to spend some time looking, but also don't stress out - it works out in the end, I'm sure.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I don't really remember now, I'm sorry. I just followed the mails that were send to me, and tried not to panic too much about the registration.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You get emails telling you what to do and when. If you just follow them, everything will work out for you <3

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful! I talked to the professors whos classes I was interested in, and they all let me take their courses.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't stress about it, everything will fall into place. Always talk to the professor, they can help you out a lot, and are often eager to get enthusiastic students, so if you really want a course, chances are in your favor.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: They were more difficult than expected. It seems very chill in the beginning, where you basically just sit and talk with the other students, but they have quite high expectations for your written assignments.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Much more emphasis on talking than writing, an interesting challenge. I'm not used to that from Copenhagen, and was not prepared for this. It was fun trying out!

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Feminisms on the move 
Migration and revolutions in the middle east 
Existentialism in political theory 
Elicitation methods in social sciences

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of them, very interesting! Lisesbeth Schoonheim particularly is a fantastic teacher, and I would take any of her courses if I could.

Personal spending DKK per month *

Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Enrollment fee from HU

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Transportation - it is part of the enrollment that you get acces to public transportation. This is very neat! 
Also the food on campus is so cheap and very good. Will recommend using that!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything is possible at HU, so many things to do! I only did some social things with HUGS, and didn't participate in anything with culture or sports through the university. But I know friends who did yoga, swimming, running, theater classes, german talking group and so on. They send out a mail with this, and you can just browse through to see if anything speaks to you.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: HUGS related things, they are very good! I met a few friends here, and I think they take you to some nice places all over Berling. They also do a campus tour, which is very helpful.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Boros Collection (a wonderful art museum with an interesting history) , Teufel See (the best sea in Berlin in my opinion!), Potsdam and the castles (worth a trip) and the Berlin nightlife (especially Sisyphos, Beathe Uwe and Heideglühen), foodmarkets in parks (the thai marked moves around a bit at the moment, but is very good and cute!).

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very similar to Copenhagen, so I didn't have any trouble.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Try to get together with the german students in group work in class. Then you know them a bit and will start talking to them in the breaks, and they will maybe invite you to socialize.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not any really, I think the culture is very similar to Copenhagen.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Very friendly classmates! I was surprises, as I heard that germans are a little more reserved. But that wasn't true in my opinion.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Don't stress about the course registration, that will work out! Just talk to the professor if you didn't get a course you wanted.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Use incoming team and hugs!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: New friends.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Money, as housing is so expensive.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
